discovery: Prediction and discovery of magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene: flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity controlled by the twist angle

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: two-dimensional van der Waals materials
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that at a 'magic' twist angle near 1.1 degrees, interlayer hybridisation in bilayer graphene produces nearly flat electronic bands. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group realised this experimentally, discovering correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity that can be switched by a gate electrode. This work made the stacking angle between atomic layers a new, continuously tunable physical parameter. It opened the field of moire quantum matter, which now includes orbital ferromagnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect, fractional Chern insulators in twisted MoTe2, and moire ferroelectricity. Few discoveries in condensed matter physics have so directly turned a simple geometric control into access to strongly correlated and topological phases in one clean, gate-tunable device. Its influence on fundamental physics and on future quantum and electronic technologies is broad and lasting.
